title: Patron's Guide: Bushels Rolled Free of the Administrative Charge in a Crop Year
content:
**What is the crop-year roll allowance?** It is a parcel of bushels rolled free of the administrative charge on Grain Marketing Contracts, and it is taken off the bushels the roll moves before the rate is applied.

**How large is it?**

- Where the net bushels of every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition, reach 15000 and eight or more such loads stand, the allowance is 5000 bushels.
- Where those net bushels reach 9000, or five or more such loads stand, the allowance is 2500 bushels.
- Where neither of those holds, no allowance is given.

**Which loads are counted?** Every load standing against the contract, whatever the disposition: a load the member directed to the contract at the scale and a load the member ran straight through to the buyer both count, and both count wherever the load was received. Their net bushels are added together, and the count of such loads is the count of all of them.

**Must both conditions be met?** In the first band, yes: 15000 net bushels and eight such loads together. In the second band, either condition is enough on its own, so 9000 net bushels on three loads reaches it, and so do five loads carrying 6,000 bushels between them.

**Are the threshold figures themselves inside the band?** Yes. Net bushels of 15000 reach the first band and 14,999 do not; 9000 reach the second and 8,999 do not; eight loads reach the first band and seven do not; five loads reach the second and four do not.

**A hypothetical case.** A contract with 18,000 net bushels standing against it on nine loads takes the 5000 bushel allowance, so an instruction moving 7,000 bushels leaves 2,000 chargeable bushels. The same contract with 10,000 net bushels on three loads takes the 2500 bushel allowance instead, leaving 4,500 chargeable bushels on the same instruction. A contract with 4,000 net bushels on two loads takes no allowance, and all 7,000 bushels are chargeable.
